metadata.description: Explore Wisconsin's state parks, forests, and recreation areas.
metadata.author: Journey

journey.name: Wisconsin State Parks
journey.description: Explore 50 remarkable state parks and recreation areas across Wisconsin, from Great Lakes shorelines and Northwoods waterfalls to Driftless bluffs and glacial landscapes.

items.name: Amnicon Falls State Park
items.description: A chain of waterfalls, rapids, rocky riverbanks, and a historic covered bridge make this compact northern park especially rewarding for short hikes and photography.

items.name: Aztalan State Park
items.description: Reconstructed platform mounds, a stockade, and riverside trails reveal the story of a major Mississippian settlement and one of Wisconsin's most significant archaeological landscapes.

items.name: Belmont Mound State Park
items.description: Wooded trails climb a prominent Driftless Area mound, where an observation tower and hilltop views create a quiet stop rich in scenery and local history.

items.name: Big Bay State Park
items.description: Madeline Island's sandstone shoreline, sandy beach, lagoon boardwalk, and island forests make the ferry trip part of an unforgettable Lake Superior adventure.

items.name: Big Foot Beach State Park
items.description: A wooded campground, prairie trails, and easy access to Geneva Lake make this southern Wisconsin park a relaxed destination for swimming, hiking, and family outings.

items.name: Blue Mound State Park
items.description: Observation towers atop southern Wisconsin's highest point overlook the Driftless landscape, while wooded trails, mountain biking, skiing, and a summer pool invite year-round exploration.

items.name: Brunet Island State Park
items.description: An island in the Chippewa River anchors a peaceful landscape of backwaters, pine forest, paddling routes, and trails connected to the Old Abe State Trail.

items.name: Buckhorn State Park
items.description: A broad peninsula on Castle Rock Lake offers beaches, boating, fishing, wildlife watching, and secluded campsites surrounded by wetlands and oak-pine forest.

items.name: Capital Springs State Recreation Area
items.description: Prairies, wetlands, lakeshore, trails, and archaeological sites create a surprisingly wild outdoor escape just minutes from downtown Madison.

items.name: Chippewa Moraine State Recreation Area
items.description: Kettle lakes, glacial ridges, forest trails, and an interpretive center showcase one of Wisconsin's finest Ice Age landscapes along the Ice Age Trail.

items.name: Copper Culture State Park
items.description: A riverside museum and ancient burial grounds interpret the Old Copper Culture, offering a meaningful blend of archaeology, woodland scenery, and Wisconsin history.

items.name: Copper Falls State Park
items.description: Waterfalls tumble through a dramatic Bad River gorge framed by ancient lava flows, forest trails, rustic stone structures, and some of northern Wisconsin's most striking scenery.

items.name: Council Grounds State Park
items.description: Quiet Wisconsin River shoreline, wooded campsites, swimming, paddling, and fishing make this small park near Merrill an inviting Northwoods retreat.

items.name: Devil's Lake State Park
items.description: Towering quartzite bluffs, balanced rock formations, scenic trails, and a clear spring-fed lake make this Wisconsin's signature outdoor destination.

items.name: Governor Dodge State Park
items.description: Two lakes, sandstone cliffs, wooded ridges, prairie, horseback trails, and Stephens Falls create one of the Driftless Area's most varied outdoor playgrounds.

items.name: Governor Nelson State Park
items.description: Prairie, oak savanna, effigy mounds, and a Lake Mendota beach offer expansive views toward Madison's skyline from the capital region's north shore.

items.name: Governor Thompson State Park
items.description: Lakes, streams, hardwood forest, and quiet trails near the Peshtigo River provide a spacious setting for camping, paddling, fishing, and Northwoods solitude.

items.name: Harrington Beach State Park
items.description: A mile of Lake Michigan beach, cedar wetlands, prairie, and a clear former quarry lake combine shoreline recreation with excellent hiking and stargazing.

items.name: Hartman Creek State Park
items.description: Spring-fed lakes, pine and hardwood forest, mountain-bike trails, swimming, and family camping make this central Wisconsin park a classic all-season getaway.

items.name: High Cliff State Park
items.description: Niagara Escarpment cliffs rise above Lake Winnebago, offering panoramic overlooks, wooded trails, effigy mounds, a marina, and memorable sunset views.

items.name: Interstate State Park
items.description: Basalt cliffs, glacial potholes, and river overlooks line the Dalles of the St. Croix at Wisconsin's oldest state park and the western end of the Ice Age Trail.

items.name: Kinnickinnic State Park
items.description: Forested bluffs overlook the meeting of the Kinnickinnic and St. Croix rivers, with sandy delta beaches, hiking, paddling, and boat-in access.

items.name: Kohler-Andrae State Park
items.description: Golden Lake Michigan beach, rolling dunes, cordwalk trails, pine forest, and a nature center create one of Wisconsin's most beautiful shoreline parks.

items.name: Lake Kegonsa State Park
items.description: Oak woodland, prairie, a swimming beach, and easy lake access make this Madison-area park ideal for relaxed camping, paddling, fishing, and winter recreation.

items.name: Lake Wissota State Park
items.description: Pine forest, restored prairie, a broad swimming beach, and access to Lake Wissota and the Old Abe State Trail support year-round recreation near Chippewa Falls.

items.name: Lakeshore State Park
items.description: An urban island and lakefront trails pair prairie habitat and fishing access with striking views of Milwaukee's skyline, harbor, and Lake Michigan.

items.name: Lizard Mound State Park
items.description: A peaceful woodland trail passes one of the nation's best-preserved collections of Indigenous effigy mounds, offering a reflective experience centered on culture and landscape.

items.name: Merrick State Park
items.description: Mississippi River backwaters surround quiet campsites and paddling channels where anglers, birders, and boaters can explore a rich floodplain landscape.

items.name: Mill Bluff State Park
items.description: Steep sandstone buttes rise from the former bed of Glacial Lake Wisconsin, creating distinctive overlooks, wooded trails, camping, and a small swimming pond.

items.name: Mirror Lake State Park
items.description: Calm, no-wake water reflects wooded sandstone cliffs, making this park especially appealing for paddling, hiking, camping, and peaceful Wisconsin Dells escapes.

items.name: Natural Bridge State Park
items.description: A short woodland hike leads to Wisconsin's largest natural arch and an ancient rock shelter used by people thousands of years ago.

items.name: Nelson Dewey State Park
items.description: High bluffs overlook the Mississippi River from the former estate of Wisconsin's first governor, with scenic hiking, camping, and nearby historic Stonefield.

items.name: New Glarus Woods State Park
items.description: Mature woodland, restored prairie, quiet campsites, and access to the Sugar River State Trail offer a relaxed base near New Glarus.

items.name: Newport State Park
items.description: Wisconsin's only designated wilderness park protects remote Lake Michigan shoreline, backpack campsites, dark skies, and miles of quiet Door County trails.

items.name: Pattison State Park
items.description: Big Manitou Falls plunges 165 feet into the Black River gorge, joined by forest trails, Little Manitou Falls, camping, and a spring-fed swimming lake.

items.name: Peninsula State Park
items.description: Limestone bluffs, shoreline trails, Eagle Bluff Lighthouse, camping, golf, and spectacular Green Bay sunsets make this Door County's landmark state park.

items.name: Perrot State Park
items.description: Steep Mississippi River bluffs, rare goat prairies, ancient earthworks, and sweeping overlooks reward hikers above the Trempealeau River valley.

items.name: Potawatomi State Park
items.description: Rocky shoreline, forest trails, camping, and views across Sturgeon Bay mark the eastern terminus of the Ice Age Trail in Door County.

items.name: Rib Mountain State Park
items.description: Trails and overlooks cross one of Wisconsin's highest and oldest rock formations, rising above Wausau with broad views and four-season recreation.

items.name: Richard Bong State Recreation Area
items.description: Prairies, wetlands, lakes, extensive trails, and unusual open-space activities fill the former site of an unfinished Air Force base in southeastern Wisconsin.

items.name: Roche-a-Cri State Park
items.description: A stairway climbs a striking sandstone outcrop marked with ancient petroglyphs, rewarding visitors with woodland trails and wide central Wisconsin views.

items.name: Rock Island State Park
items.description: Two ferry rides lead to a vehicle-free island of primitive campsites, rugged shoreline, historic stone buildings, and Wisconsin's oldest lighthouse.

items.name: Rocky Arbor State Park
items.description: Shaded sandstone walls, mossy ravines, and a compact campground provide a quiet natural refuge just outside busy Wisconsin Dells.

items.name: Straight Lake State Park
items.description: A remote lake, mature forest, glacial terrain, primitive camping, and the Ice Age Trail create a quiet destination for hiking, paddling, and solitude.

items.name: Tower Hill State Park
items.description: A wooded trail climbs to a reconstructed shot tower above the Wisconsin River, blending industrial history, scenic overlooks, and Driftless Area hiking.

items.name: Whitefish Dunes State Park
items.description: Wisconsin's tallest sand dunes, broad Lake Michigan beach, forest trails, and a nature center preserve a remarkable Door County shoreline landscape.

items.name: Wildcat Mountain State Park
items.description: Wooded ridges rise above the winding Kickapoo River, offering bluff-top views, hiking, horseback trails, paddling access, and Driftless Area camping.

items.name: Willow River State Park
items.description: Willow Falls cascades through a sandstone gorge below wooded trails, lakeside camping, fishing, and easy access from the Twin Cities region.

items.name: Wyalusing State Park
items.description: High wooded bluffs overlook the meeting of the Wisconsin and Mississippi rivers, with panoramic trails, Native American mounds, camping, and rich birdlife.

items.name: Yellowstone Lake State Park
items.description: A broad Driftless Area reservoir supports swimming, paddling, fishing, camping, wildlife viewing, and rolling trails through woods and prairie.
